This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.
S.A.Ravishankara S/o Appajappa in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that:-
 That the 1st petitioner is the father and 2 nd and 3rd petitioners are the brothers of deceased Ravishankara.

On 17.03.2018 at about 12.40 pm the deceased on his duty hours and while he was proceeding as a pedestrian on the left side of Nice Road, Under Pass Turn, Ring Road Junction on the left side of the road, at that time the driver of Mahindra DI 3200 BS III Brg.Reg.No.KA-41-A-9264 came from Mysore Ring Road to go to Nice Road Toll with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the deceased and caused Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
2 the accident.
Due to impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to death on the spot.
Thereafter Post Mortem was conducted and the body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent more than Rs.50,000/- towards conveyance, food and nourishment charges, transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremonies.

Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy,
aged about 28 years, he was Police Constable and earning  SCCH-9 4 MVC.No.3187/2018 Rs.25.773/- p.m.

The petitioners have lost all his income and he was contributing his entire income to the family and he was only bread earner of their family and all the family members were depending upon on the income of the deceased for their livelihood.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Mahindra vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-A-9264.
The Byatarajayanpura Police have registered a Criminal Case against the driver of offending vehicle in Cr.No.25/2018 for the offence punishable U/Sec. 279, 304 (A) of IPC.
After investigation the Police have filed Charge Sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/sec 304A of IPC.
The respondents being Owner and Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners who lost their bread earner in the accident.

Hence, petitioners constrained to file Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
3
a petition for compensation.
3. After service of notice the respondent No.1 did not choose to file its written statement.
The respondent  SCCH-9 5 MVC.No.3187/2018 No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed its objection/written statement.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is as under:
This respondent has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance Policy to Mahindra Goods vehicle Reg.No.KA-41-A-9264 vide GCV Public Carrier other than 3-wheeler package Policy No.0701013117P07878700 for the period from 08.07.2017 to 07.09.2018 and the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically denies the occurrence of accident, mode of accident, age of deceased, avocation and income of deceased and also involvement of vehicle i.e., Reg.No.KA-41-A-9264.

This respondent further contended that petitioners have filed false case with an intention to cause wrongful gain from this respondent and the concern police without investigation by colluding with the complainant filed false Charge Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
This respondent  SCCH-9 6 MVC.No.3187/2018 has also denies the relationship of the petitioners with that of the deceased.

It has also contended that the driver of Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
4 Mahindra vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-A-9264 was not having valid and effective driving license, valid Permit, FC to ply on public road.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.
This respondent specifically contended that only to get the compensation the offending vehicle is implicated in this case.
The offending vehicle driver has not at all caused the accident.
This respondent specifically contended that alleged accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased himself.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, this respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed:
 ISSUES  1.
Whether petitioners prove that, on  28.08.2017 at about 12.00 noon, Ravishankar  was on his duty hours was pedestrian on the  left side of Nice Road Under Pass Turn, Ring  Road junction.

At that time suddenly driver of  Mahindra D13200 BSIII Brg.Reg.No.KA-41-A-  9264 came from Mysore Road, Ring Road to go  SCCH-9 7 MVC.No.3187/2018  to Nice Road, in a rash and negligent manner  with high speed without observing traffic rules  and regulations and dashed against the  Ravishankara.
Consequent to which  Ravishankara sustained grievous injuries and  died on spot?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation as claimed?

If so, to what  amount and from whom?
 3.
What order or award?

5  5.

In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.2 himself examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15 and in support of their case they have examined Investigating Officer by name H.R.Balakrishnaraju as PW2, Home Guard by name T.J.Venkobha Rao as PW3 and got marked document at Ex.P16 & 17 and eye witness Dr.Rajesh as PW4 and got marked document Ex.P18 & 19.
On the other hand, the Administrative Officer/insurance company was examined as RW1 and got marked Ex.R1 & 2 and closed the side.
6. I have heard the arguments of both side and perused the materials available on record.
The counsel for petitioners have filed written argument.

7. My answer to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.1:-

It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 17.03.2018 at about 12.40 afternoon.,
the deceased S.A.Ravishankara met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-A-9264.
Due to impact deceased was succumbed to death.

The respondents being owner and insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners who have lost their Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
6 bread earner in the accident.

sentences.text: 9. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.2 himself examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination by reiterating all the facts mentioned in the petition.
He also relied documents at Ex.P1 to P15.

The Ex.P1 is the FIR & complaint, Ex.P2 is the Further statement of complainant, Ex.P3 is the Spot Panchanama, Ex.P4 is the  SCCH-9 9 MVC.No.3187/2018 Spot Sketch, Ex.P5 is the IMV Report, Ex.P6 is the Inquest Report, Ex.P7 is the Post Mortem Report, Ex.P8 is the charge sheet, Ex.P9 is the Pay Slip of deceased, Ex.P10 is the Notarized copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1 & 2,
Ex.P11 is the Succession certificate, Ex.P12 is Notarized copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner, Ex.P13 is the Notarized copy of Aadhaar card of deceased and Ex.P14 & 15 are the ID card of deceased.
10. As stated above the petitioners contended that accident in question was caused by the driver of the offending vehicle.

The 2nd respondent, who is the insurer of the offending vehicle has strongly opposed the petition and mainly contended that the offending vehicle is implicated subsequently, after the accident to get the compensation.
When serious dispute about involvement of the vehicle it is the petitioners to prove that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.

In order to prove the said fact, the petitioner No.2, who is the brother of the deceased has filed Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
7 affidavit in lieu of chief examination and stated the cause of the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for 2nd respondent has  SCCH-9 10 MVC.No.3187/2018 vehemently cross-examined the PW1 but nothing was elicited to disbelieve his evidence.
Apart from this, the petitioners in order to prove the involvement of the vehicle and negligence of the driver has examined the Investigating Officer as PW2.
The PW2 in his chief-examination stated in detail about the conduct of the investigation.

He has specifically stated that on the basis of CCTV footage, which is fixed on the building of one Mahaveer and on the basis of statement of owner of the said building traced out the vehicle and filed the charge sheet.
This PW2 was also elaborately cross-examined by the learned counsel for 2nd respondent but nothing was elicited to disbelieve his evidence.
The petitioners also examined 1st informant/complainant as PW3 who circustancial witness.
The said PW3 in his chief-examination clearly stated that he was on duty along with deceased Ravishankar near Nice Road turning Veerabadranagar Signal Point to control the traffic.
When deceased went to nature call and at 12.40 p.m., one person came to his place and told deceased met with an accident near Nice Road turning.
Thereafter, he  SCCH-9 11 MVC.No.3187/2018 rushed into the accident place and saw the dead body of the deceased.

He was elaborately cross-examined by the Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
8 learned counsel for 2nd respondent but nothing was elicited to disbelieve his evidence.

The material eye witness also examined as PW4 and this PW4 in his chief-examination affidavit clearly stated that when he was driving his car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MX-2389 to go to Mysuru he saw the driver of Goods Tempo, who was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently without observing the traffic rules and regulations, he also stated that the said Goods vehicle hit to the Traffic Police Constable, who was pedestrian walking on the left side.
This PW4 was elaborately cross-examined by the learned counsel for 2nd respondent but nothing was elicited to disbelieve this evidence.
11 . Further it is material to note that in the FIR, there is no mention of vehicle number.
However, while submitting the charge sheet the I.O has mentioned vehicle number as No.KA-41-9264.

The Police records shows that initially the FIR was registered against the unknown vehicle and after investigation charge sheet is filed against the driver of  SCCH-9 12 MVC.No.3187/2018 offending vehicle.
The Investigating Officer has clearly stated that on the basis of CCTV footage they traced out the vehicle and seized the same and filed the charge sheet.
The 2nd respondent contended that the offending vehicle was falsely implicated in this case.

But the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioners clearly goes to show that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident and the driver of offending vehicle has caused the Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
9 alleged accident.

entities.text: Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Ex.P3/hand sketch also clearly goes to show that the place of accident is the Ring Road in Nice Road.
Apart from this the entire police records especially charge sheet leveled charges for the offence punishable U/sec 279 and 304A IPC.
Therefore, the contention of 2 nd respondent that vehicle is falsely implicated and there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle cannot be sustain at all.

12 . Moreover in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal  SCCH-9 13 MVC.No.3187/2018 case.
This principles of law was laid down by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).

The 2nd respondent examined its administrative officer as RW1 but he is not a eyewitness and mere self swearing statement is not sufficient without document to hold the offending vehicle is falsely implicated in this case and there was no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the oral and documentary evidence adduced by petitioners clearly establishes that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Now it can safely be conclude, deceased was dead due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
10 offending vehicle.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved issue No.1.
Hence, I answered issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. ISSUE No.2: Therefore, in view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income  SCCH-9 14 MVC.No.3187/2018 of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies,
towards loss of love and affection, etc., let me discuss one by one.
(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
In the petition the age of deceased Ravishankara has shown as 28 years.
The petitioners produced Ex.P13 Aadhaar card of deceased which shows his date of birth as 01.05.1988., whereas date of accident is 17.03.2018.
According to Aadhar card, the age of deceased at the time of accident was 30 years.
In Pranay Sethi and others Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the age of the deceased is to be considered for applying multiplier.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarala Verma case "17" multiplier is applicable in present case.
I) The petitioners contended that deceased was serving as Police Constable and drawing salary of Rs.25,773/- per month.

In this regard, they have produced Ex.P9/salary slip of deceased for the month of February- Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
11 2018.

entities.text: Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said Ex.P9 it has mentioned gross salary amounting to Rs.25,773/- and after deduction of  SCCH-9 15 MVC.No.3187/2018 Professional Tax of Rs.200/-, it would comes Rs.25,573/-.
Even it is material to note that there is no serious dispute about avocation of the deceased.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.25,573/- is considered as monthly income of deceased to assess the compensation.
ii) In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

In Pranaya Sethi and other Case the Hon'be Supreme Court held that in case the deceased was having permanent job an addition of 50% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was below age of 40 years.
Case on hand deceased was aged about 30 years and he was having permanent job.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 50% of salary to the established income.
The established income of the deceased is Rs.25,573/- and 50% of Rs.25,573/- it would comes Rs.12,786/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased is Rs.25,573 + Rs.12,786 = Rs.38,359/- p.m.

Admittedly deceased was a bachelor, hence as per ratio laid down by  SCCH-9 16 MVC.No.3187/2018 the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the above reported judgments 50% of income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal expenses and 50% is to be Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
12 taken as dependency and it would comes Rs.19,180/- p.m.
The 1st petitioner is the father and 2nd & 3rd petitioners are the elder brothers of deceased.
The petitioner No.2 & 3 being major elder brothers are not entitled for any compensation and moreover they cannot be considered as dependent of the deceased.

In this regard, I would like to rely judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court New India Insurance Co. V/s Anand Pal, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court was please to held at Para No.5 and 8 as under:
 "In the absence of evidence to the contrary,
 brothers and sisters will not be considered as  dependents as because they will either be  independent and earning, or married, or be  dependent on the father.

entities.text: Apex Court New India Insurance Co. V/s Anand Pal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Looking at the above, the Tribunal and the  High Court should not have considered the three  older married siblings, to be dependent on the  deceased victim.
The compensation awarded to  the married siblings is therefore found to be  unmerited.

The appeal is accordingly allowed by  setting aside the impugned award of the Motor  Accident Claims Tribunal as upheld by the High  Court under the impugned judgment."
 SCCH-9 17 MVC.No.3187/2018
Thus petitioner No.1 is only entitled to compensation of Rs.39,12,720/-= (19,180/-X12XM17) towards loss of dependency.
(B) Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses;

In view of Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others in Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020 & in between National Insurance Company LTD V/s Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
13

Thus, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation as follows:

 loss of future  earnings.

In respect of interest is concerned, in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1)
 of the Act to the extent they speak of interest  payable on the compensation amount is in the  nature of an exception to the general law  enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the  provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent  become invocable on the general principles of  construction of statutes namely the special law  overrides the general law.
Therefore, in the  absence of any other law relating to interest on  Judgments, the MACT has to follow the  provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
14  the given circumstances of this case, interest at  the rate of more than 6% could not have been  awarded."

Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
14

sentences.text:
In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
 SCCH-9 19 MVC.No.3187/2018
15. REGARDING LIABILITY:
The 2nd respondent has contended that policy issued in favour of respondent No.1 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
On perusal of entire materials available on record there is no material is available to show that the respondent No.1, who is the owner of offending vehicle has violated the conditions of the policy.
Even the 2nd respondent has not at all established 1st respondent has violated terms and conditions of the policy.
Under such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer are liable to pay the compensation.
As already stated above, the accident in question was caused by the driver of offending vehicle by rash and negligent driving of the vehicle.
The petitioners have proved that the accident was caused by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Under such circumstances, the respondent No.1 and 2 are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner No1.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its Appajappa vs Sudha A.S on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182057138/
15  SCCH-9 20 MVC.No.3187/2018 realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation of Rs.39,82,720/- (Rupees Thirty Nine Lakhs Eighty Two Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty Only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner No.1.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the total compensation amount, 50% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 and remaining 50% of the amount shall be deposited in his name in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru for a period of three years.
He is entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The 2nd respondent, who is the insurer of the offending vehicle has strongly opposed the petition and mainly contended that the offending vehicle is implicated subsequently, after the accident to get the compensation.
When serious dispute about involvement of the vehicle it is the petitioners to prove that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.

Therefore, the contention of 2 nd respondent that vehicle is falsely implicated and there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle cannot be sustain at all.
12 . Moreover in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal  SCCH-9 13 MVC.No.3187/2018 case.
This principles of law was laid down by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).
Therefore, the oral and documentary evidence adduced by petitioners clearly establishes that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

16. Issue No.3:
For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation of Rs.39,82,720/- (Rupees Thirty Nine Lakhs Eighty Two Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty Only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner No.1.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, 50% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 and remaining 50% of the amount shall be deposited in his name in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru for a period of three years.
He is entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
